name: Bellhop job lifecycle
description: A job from enqueue to removal: scheduling, uniqueness, claiming, leases and recovery, success, retries and dead-lettering, cancellation, timeouts, routing, queues, priority, concurrency keys, rate limits, continuations, chains, batches, retention, captured logs, tags and correlation. Node lifecycle and health are in the hosting module; recurring definitions are in the recurring module.

entities.name: Job
entities.description: One stored job: a stable name, a JSON payload and its execution state.

entities.name: Queue
entities.description: A named queue that workers drain.

entities.name: Batch
entities.description: A named group of jobs created atomically, with batch-level continuations.

entities.name: Throttle
entities.description: A concurrency key (mutex or semaphore) or a rate-limit key enforced by the store across nodes.

ears.shall: retry a failing job up to MaxAttempts = 5 attempts in total by default, with exponential backoff and jitter of roughly 10 s, 1 min, 5 min and 30 min between attempts, configurable globally, per job type and per enqueue

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: per-enqueue options beat the job type's settings, which beat the global default (see INV-123 for attribute versus fluent).

ears.shall: use the stable job name from [JobName], or the type's simple name when none is given, as the job's identity in storage, and treat each alias listed on [JobName] as the same job
give every claim a lease of LeaseDuration, 60 seconds by default, and renew it by heartbeat every LeaseDuration / 3 (HeartbeatInterval)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: 60 s, so heartbeats run every 20 s. The docs state it as the duplicate window (EXE-5, REQ-10).

ears.shall: poll for work at PollInterval, 1 second by default, when no notification mechanism wakes the node (PollInterval)
retain jobs per state for RetentionSucceeded = 7 days, RetentionCancelled = 7 days and RetentionDeadLettered = 30 days by default

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 (§9 Q5): Succeeded jobs are kept 7 days instead of 24 h, for more debugging history at the cost of a larger table.

ears.shall: apply a payload soft limit of PayloadSoftLimit = 64 KB and a hard limit of PayloadHardLimit = 1 MB by default

requirements.notes: The Redis store lowers the hard limit to 256 KB (REQ-513).

ears.shall: default a node's concurrency limit to 2 × ProcessorCount (NodeConcurrency)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: 2 × ProcessorCount, without the floor of 8 the source proposed. A 1-CPU container therefore runs 2 jobs at once by default; the docs should say so for I/O-bound workloads.

sources.quote: proposal: max(8, 2 × ProcessorCount)

ears.shall: treat Scheduled, Enqueued, Processing, Awaiting, Failed and Unroutable as the active states for uniqueness, and Ignore as the default duplicate policy

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: a unique key is held until the job is Succeeded, DeadLettered or Cancelled, so no duplicate can appear while the first job waits for a retry or a handler. Widens SCH-5's list.

sources.quote: an active job (Scheduled, Enqueued, Processing, Awaiting) with the same key exists

ears.shall: give every job a priority of 0 unless one is set, and capture log lines at Information level and above, up to CapturedLogLimit = 256 KB per job, by default
remove expired jobs in batches of at most CleanupBatchSize = 500 rows with a short pause between batches

ears.when: an application enqueues a job
ears.shall: store the job as enqueued and return its job id

sources.quote: EnqueueAsync(job, options?) runs as soon as a worker is free. Returns a JobId.

ears.when: an application schedules a job for a point in time or after a delay that is still in the future according to the database clock
ears.shall: store the job as scheduled with scheduledAt set to that time, or to now plus the delay, and return its job id

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: a time that is not in the future is REQ-182.

ears.when: its scheduledAt has passed according to the database clock
ears.shall: move the job to enqueued

ears.while: a job is enqueued in an active queue that is below its concurrency limit, the maintenance pause is off, its concurrency key and rate limit admit it and, for a job tagged LongRunning, the node is below its LongRunning limit
ears.when: a running node with the worker registered and a handler for the job's name or one of its aliases holds claims on fewer processing jobs than its concurrency limit and the job is the next one by queue order and priority
ears.shall: claim the job for that worker, record the claiming node, issue a new leaseToken, increment the attempt number and set leaseExpiresAt to the database time plus LeaseDuration

requirements.notes: The attempt number is counted at claim time; that is what makes EXE-4 'attempt counted' hold for interrupted runs. Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: only nodes with the worker registered claim (hosting REQ-20), a node claims only jobs it has a handler for (REQ-124), and every claim gets a fresh lease token (INV-128). Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-2 (recommended option): the queue limit (INV-107) and the LongRunning limit (INV-112) are claim conditions here, not only in INV-107's notes. Run 2 F-7 (recommended option): 'a free worker slot' is now spelled out as fewer claims than the node's concurrency limit, the measure INV-106 uses, so a handler whose lease was lost does not keep a slot; REQ-191 records it instead.

sources.quote: A job can be claimed by exactly one worker using store-native primitives. Claims carry a lease with an expiry.

ears.when: it has been enqueued for longer than UnroutableAfter
ears.if: no running worker node lists a handler for its name or any of its aliases
ears.shall: mark the job unroutable without failing, retrying or deleting it

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: nodes publish their handler names with their heartbeat and claim only jobs they can run (REQ-123). A sweep marks a job Unroutable only when it has waited UnroutableAfter and no live node lists its name, so a node without the handler during a rolling deploy never parks a job another node can run, and a long backlog never triggers it.

sources.quote: Jobs whose name has no registered handler MUST enter an Unroutable state, visible in the dashboard, and MUST NOT be failed or deleted.

ears.when: a running worker node registers a handler for its name or one of its aliases
ears.shall: return the job to enqueued

sources.quote: They resume automatically when a handler appears.

ears.when: HeartbeatInterval has passed since the last renewal
ears.shall: extend leaseExpiresAt by LeaseDuration without any action by the handler

ears.when: its handler returns without an exception
ears.shall: mark the job succeeded

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: a run whose lease was taken over cannot complete the job; see INV-128.

ears.when: its handler returns without an exception
ears.if: the job returns a result no larger than ResultSizeLimit
ears.shall: store the result so it can be read by job id

requirements.notes: Same event as REQ-127 with a second consequence. Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: ResultSizeLimit is 1 MB (REQ-185); a larger result is REQ-184.

ears.while: a job is processing and its cancellation was not requested
ears.when: its handler throws an exception
ears.if: the exception is not an OperationCanceledException thrown after the job's token was cancelled for shutdown, and the attempt number is below maxAttempts and the retry policy allows another attempt
ears.shall: mark the job failed and set retryAt from the backoff

requirements.notes: Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-7: a job whose cancellation was requested is marked cancelled instead (REQ-190). F-8: an OperationCanceledException after the shutdown signal is REQ-140, not a failed attempt.

ears.when: its retryAt has passed according to the database clock
ears.shall: move the job to enqueued

sources.quote: Failed (will retry)

ears.when: its handler throws an exception
ears.if: the exception is not an OperationCanceledException thrown after the job's token was cancelled for shutdown, and the attempt number has reached maxAttempts, the retry policy declines another attempt, or the exception is a PermanentJobFailureException
ears.shall: move the job to dead-lettered

requirements.notes: Same event as REQ-129; the guards are complementary, so exactly one of the two applies. PermanentJobFailureException skips retries (RET-2). Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-8: an OperationCanceledException after the shutdown signal is REQ-140, not a failure. Run 2 F-1 (recommended option): this applies whether or not cancellation was requested; REQ-190 takes only the failures that would have been retried.

sources.quote: When attempts are exhausted the job MUST move to DeadLettered

ears.while: a job is processing and its cancellation was not requested
ears.when: its leaseExpiresAt has passed according to the database clock
ears.if: the attempt number is below maxAttempts
ears.shall: let any running worker node return the job to enqueued with reason Interrupted, keeping the attempt counted

requirements.notes: Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-7: a job whose cancellation was requested is marked cancelled instead (REQ-190). REQ-133 is unchanged: a dead-lettered job does not run again.

sources.quote: When a lease expires (node crash, network partition) the job MUST be returned to Enqueued with the attempt counted and reason Interrupted, or dead-lettered if attempts are exhausted. Recovery is performed by any live node

ears.when: its leaseExpiresAt has passed according to the database clock
ears.if: the attempt number has reached maxAttempts
ears.shall: let any running worker node move the job to dead-lettered with reason Interrupted

requirements.notes: Same event as REQ-132 with the complementary guard.

ears.when: an application or operator cancels a job that is scheduled, enqueued, awaiting, failed or unroutable
ears.shall: mark the job cancelled immediately

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: every job that is not finished and not Processing is cancelled at once. Processing is REQ-135 and REQ-136.

ears.when: an application or operator cancels it
ears.shall: record the cancellation request and signal the handler's cancellation token on whichever node runs the job

sources.quote: MUST signal the CancellationToken of a Processing job on whichever node runs it (cross-node)

ears.while: a job is processing and its cancellation was requested
ears.when: its handler throws OperationCanceledException
ears.shall: mark the job cancelled

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: the outcome follows the handler. If it returns normally the job is Succeeded (REQ-127), because the work was done; any other exception takes the normal failure path (REQ-129, REQ-131); if it ignores the token it stays Processing until its timeout, if it has one. Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-6/F-7: a cancelled job is never retried. If the handler throws another exception, ignores the token past a timeout, loses its lease or is released at shutdown, REQ-190 marks it cancelled instead of returning it to enqueued or failed. A normal return still marks it succeeded (REQ-127).

ears.when: it has run for longer than its timeout
ears.shall: signal the handler's cancellation token

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: every job has a timeout, 5 minutes unless one is set (REQ-189). Long-running jobs must set a longer one.

ears.while: a job is processing, its timeout token was signalled and its cancellation was not requested
ears.if: the handler is still running TimeoutGracePeriod later or throws OperationCanceledException within it, and the attempt number is below maxAttempts and the retry policy allows another attempt
ears.shall: abandon the handler if it is still running, mark the job failed with reason Timeout and set retryAt from the backoff

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: TimeoutGracePeriod is 30 s (REQ-187) and a timeout is an ordinary failed attempt: it is retried, or dead-lettered when attempts run out (REQ-186). An abandoned handler keeps running in the process; lease fencing (INV-128) makes its eventual result harmless. Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-6 (recommended option): a job whose cancellation was requested is never retried; REQ-136 or REQ-190 marks it cancelled.

sources.quote: a handler that ignores cancellation is abandoned after a grace period and the job is marked Failed with reason Timeout

ears.when: ShutdownTimeout has passed and the job is still running
ears.shall: signal the handler's cancellation token

ears.while: the job's node is draining, the job's token was cancelled for shutdown and its cancellation was not requested
ears.if: the handler is still running, or it throws OperationCanceledException and its timeout token was not signalled
ears.shall: release the job's lease and take back the attempt it counted, so another node can claim it immediately and the interrupted run does not count towards maxAttempts

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: shutdown is not the job's fault, so the attempt is not counted; a crash (lease expiry, REQ-132) still counts. The lease is released as soon as ShutdownTimeout passes. The old handler may still run in the stopping process while another node claims the job; that is an expected at-least-once duplicate, and fencing (INV-128) refuses its result. Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-8 (recommended option): a handler that honours the shutdown token by throwing OperationCanceledException is released the same way as one that ignores it, so cooperating never costs an attempt. F-7: a job whose cancellation was requested is marked cancelled instead (REQ-190). Run 2 F-2 (recommended option): an OperationCanceledException thrown after both the timeout and the shutdown signal is a timeout (REQ-138, REQ-186), so the attempt counts and a job that keeps timing out during rolling deploys still uses up its attempts.

sources.quote: then any still-running jobs have their leases released so another node picks them up immediately

ears.when: an operator requeues a dead-lettered job through the API or the dashboard
ears.shall: enqueue the job again with its attempt number reset to zero and its cancellation request cleared

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 run 2 F-4 (recommended option): a requeue is a fresh start, so a cancellation requested during an earlier run does not turn the next run's first failure into a cancel (REQ-190, REQ-136).

ears.when: an operator requeues dead-lettered jobs in bulk by name, queue, tag or time range
ears.shall: enqueue each matching dead-lettered job again in its own atomic step with its attempt number reset to zero and its cancellation request cleared, skip any job whose unique key is held by another active job, and return how many were requeued, how many were skipped because their state changed meanwhile and how many were skipped because their unique key is held

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: per job, not all-or-nothing, so a large set never holds one long transaction. Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-4 (recommended option): the unique-key guard of INV-129 applies per job in bulk requeue, with its own count. Run 2 F-4: the cancellation request is cleared, as in REQ-141.

ears.when: an application or operator requeues a succeeded or cancelled job
ears.shall: enqueue the same job again with its attempt number reset to zero and its cancellation request cleared, keeping its earlier history

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: RequeueAsync(id) accepts any finished state (DeadLettered is REQ-141) and refuses the rest (INV-129). refiner-model 2026-11-06 run 2 F-4: the cancellation request is cleared, as in REQ-141. Run 2 F-6 (recommended option, accepted): requeuing a cancelled job runs that job only. Continuations cancelled with it (REQ-173, REQ-174, REQ-175) stay cancelled and must be re-created; a cancel is deliberate and ends the chain below it.

ears.when: an application or operator deletes a job
ears.shall: remove the job with its history, captured logs and parameters, and log the removal

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: any state except Processing, which must be cancelled first (INV-130). Continuations awaiting the deleted job are cancelled (REQ-188). An explicit, logged delete of a dead letter is not the silent deletion RET-3 forbids.

ears.when: a job has been succeeded, cancelled or dead-lettered for longer than that state's retention
ears.if: the job is not a member of a batch that is open or completed
ears.shall: remove the job together with its state history, captured logs and parameters, in batches of at most CleanupBatchSize

requirements.notes: Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-10 (recommended option): retention never removes a member of a batch that is not succeeded, so the batch can still complete (REQ-180) or be upgraded to succeeded (REQ-179, SCN-119). Run 2 F-5: the exemption ends when the batch itself is removed together with its members (REQ-192).

sources.quote: state history and logs follow the job

ears.when: an application enqueues a job
ears.shall: run the handler on the caller's thread before the enqueue call returns and rethrow any handler exception to the caller

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: Inline mode runs a job once with no retries (INV-131), runs continuations inline (INV-132), stores scheduled jobs without running them (INV-133) and applies unique and concurrency keys (INV-134).

ears.when: an application enqueues or schedules a job whose payload is larger than PayloadSoftLimit and not larger than PayloadHardLimit
ears.shall: store the job and log a warning with its size

ears.if: an application enqueues or schedules a job whose payload is larger than PayloadHardLimit
ears.shall: reject the call with an exception that names the size and the limit, and store nothing

sources.quote: a hard limit (default 1 MB) with a clear exception

ears.when: an application enqueues, schedules or otherwise creates a job (including a continuation, a chain step or a batch member) with a unique key while an active job with the same key exists
ears.if: the duplicate policy is Ignore, or the policy is ReplaceSchedule and the call does not schedule a job
ears.shall: create no job and return the existing job's id with WasDuplicate set to true

requirements.notes: Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-3 (recommended option): the duplicate rules cover every call that creates a job, including recurring occurrences, so INV-100 cannot be bypassed by scheduling, by ReplaceSchedule on enqueue, or by a continuation, chain step or batch member. ReplaceSchedule on a call that does not schedule behaves like Ignore, as INV-135 does for a holder that is no longer scheduled. Same event as REQ-152 with complementary guards. Open for the owner: what a chain or batch does with the other steps when one step is ignored as a duplicate.

ears.when: an application schedules a job with a unique key while a scheduled job with the same key exists
ears.if: the duplicate policy is ReplaceSchedule
ears.shall: move the existing job's scheduledAt to the new time, leave its payload unchanged, create no job and return the existing job's id with WasDuplicate set to true

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: only the time moves. An existing job that is no longer Scheduled is INV-135.

sources.quote: ReplaceSchedule (debounce: move the existing scheduled job to the new time)

ears.when: an application enqueues, schedules or otherwise creates a job (including a continuation, a chain step or a batch member) with a unique key while an active job with the same key exists
ears.if: the duplicate policy is Error
ears.shall: reject the call with an error and create no job

requirements.notes: Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-3 (recommended option): covers every call that creates a job; for a chain or batch, rejecting the call creates none of its jobs (REQ-176, REQ-177 are one transaction).

ears.shall: never hold two active jobs with the same unique key in the same namespace or, where the Redis ShardByQueue mode is on (redis INV-500), in the same queue, even when the enqueues arrive concurrently on different nodes

requirements.notes: In the Redis ShardByQueue mode the scope is per queue instead (INV-500). Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 redis F-10 (recommended option): the ShardByQueue scope is part of the sentence, not only of the notes. Every job-creating call is covered by REQ-150/REQ-152 (F-3) and bulk requeue by REQ-142 (F-4).

sources.quote: Uniqueness MUST be enforced by the store (unique index), not by read-then-write.

ears.when: an application enqueues a job inside its open database transaction
ears.shall: make the job visible to workers only if that transaction commits

ears.if: an application passes a database transaction to a store that does not support transactional enqueue
ears.shall: reject the call with an error that names the transactional-enqueue capability and the store, and store nothing

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: rejecting is the only reading that keeps INV-101; the Redis and in-memory stores report the capability as missing (REQ-512).

ears.when: an application enqueues several jobs in one bulk call
ears.shall: store either all of them or none of them

sources.quote: Bulk operations (EnqueueManyAsync) MUST be atomic

ears.when: a handler enqueues or schedules a job
ears.shall: set the new job's parentId to the running job and carry over the running job's trace context

ears.when: an application waits for a job's completion with a timeout
ears.shall: return as soon as the job is succeeded, dead-lettered or cancelled, or when the timeout passes, whichever comes first
never let more than one worker hold an unexpired claim on the same job

sources.quote: A job can be claimed by exactly one worker

ears.while: a processing job's leaseExpiresAt has not passed
ears.shall: never recover, requeue or dead-letter the job for lease expiry, however long it has been running

requirements.rationale: Recovery keys off the lease deadline, never the original fetch time, so a healthy long-running job is never requeued.

ears.shall: decide claims, lease expiry and due times against the database clock, never a node's local clock

sources.quote: Claims and due-checks MUST use the database clock

ears.shall: never hold claims on more processing jobs at once on a node than the node's concurrency limit

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-5: the limit counts claims, not handler code still executing. A handler abandoned after its timeout (REQ-138, REQ-186) or released at shutdown (REQ-140) keeps running in the process but no longer holds a claim, so it runs outside the limit; REQ-191 makes it visible. So does a handler whose lease was lost (run 2 F-7).

ears.where: a queue has a concurrency limit
ears.shall: never run more jobs from that queue at once, across all nodes, than its limit

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: cluster-wide, enforced by the store at claim time like concurrency keys. Per-node capacity is the node concurrency limit (INV-106).

ears.shall: never admit a claim that would make more jobs with the same concurrency key processing at once, across all nodes, than that key's Max at the time of the claim

requirements.notes: Max = 1 is a distributed mutex; Max = N a semaphore. Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-1 (recommended option): a rule about claims, not a state invariant, because lowering Max at runtime (REQ-158) leaves the current holders running above the new Max.

ears.while: a job's concurrency key is held by Max processing jobs or its rate limit is used up for the current window
ears.shall: keep the job enqueued and never fail it, retry it or count an attempt for waiting

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: a job blocked by a rate limit waits like one blocked by a concurrency key, and a blocked job never stalls the queue: lower-priority jobs that are allowed to run proceed (INV-111).

sources.quote: Jobs blocked by a key wait in the queue; they are never failed for waiting.

ears.where: a concurrency key is a template such as tenant:{TenantId}
ears.shall: fill the key from the job's payload properties at enqueue

ears.where: a rate limit of N executions per fixed or sliding window is set for a key
ears.shall: never start a job with that key when N jobs with that key have already started in the current window, across all nodes, counting every start including retries and recovery restarts

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: every start counts, because each one reaches the downstream system. Waiting is REQ-156. Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-1 (recommended option): a rule about starts, so lowering N at runtime (REQ-158) does not retroactively violate it for starts already made in the window.

ears.when: an operator changes a concurrency key's Max or a rate limit through the API or the Throttles page
ears.shall: apply the new limit to every following claim on every node without a redeploy, and leave jobs already running untouched

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: when Max is lowered below the current holders, they keep running and no new holder is admitted until the count drops below the new Max.

sources.quote: a limit can be changed at runtime from the API or the Throttles page without redeploying

ears.where: a worker uses strict queue priority, which is the default
ears.shall: claim from the first queue in the worker's ordered list before any later queue, as long as the first has a claimable job

requirements.notes: Strict priority can starve later queues indefinitely; LIV-100 is written to make the model report it.

sources.quote: order is the documented strict priority (first listed is drained first)

ears.where: a worker is configured for weighted round-robin
ears.shall: claim from its queues in proportion to their weights instead of strict order
claim jobs within one queue, among those its concurrency key and rate limit admit, by highest priority first and, for equal priority, in the order they were enqueued

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: a job blocked by its key or rate limit is skipped, so it never blocks lower-priority jobs behind it.

ears.where: a separate LongRunning limit is configured
ears.shall: never run more jobs tagged LongRunning at once on a node than that limit

ears.when: an operator pauses a queue through the API or the dashboard
ears.shall: mark the queue paused

ears.when: an operator resumes a paused queue through the API or the dashboard
ears.shall: mark the queue active
never claim a job from that queue

requirements.notes: Jobs already processing keep running; scheduled jobs are still promoted into the paused queue and wait there. Both are readings, not stated.

ears.when: an operator turns on the global maintenance pause
ears.shall: mark maintenance on

sources.quote: A global "maintenance" pause MUST exist.

ears.when: an operator turns off the global maintenance pause
ears.shall: mark maintenance off
never claim any job on any node

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: maintenance stops claims (here) and recurring triggers (recurring module). Promotion of scheduled jobs, lease recovery and cleanup keep running, so state stays correct and nothing piles up unseen.

ears.shall: promote each due scheduled or failed job exactly once however many worker nodes run, without relying on leader election for correctness

ears.when: retention cleanup runs
ears.shall: let at most one worker node clean up at a time by holding a short cleanup lease in the store

sources.quote: Cleanup MAY use a short lease to avoid redundant work.

ears.while: a job is enqueued in an active queue, maintenance is off and at least one running worker node serves its queue
ears.shall: eventually claim the job

requirements.notes: Not stated as such; follows from SCH-1 'runs as soon as a worker is free'. Expected to fail under strict queue priority (INV-110), under a permanently held concurrency key, or behind a stream of higher-priority jobs. That is the finding we want the model to report. Fails by design under strict queue priority (INV-110) and job priority (INV-111) when higher-ranked work arrives continuously; weighted round-robin (REQ-159) avoids it. Holds for one queue with equal priorities. Confirmed by the model 2026-11-06 (F-12); accepted by the owner.

ears.while: a job is processing and its lease has expired
ears.shall: eventually return it to enqueued or dead-letter it, provided at least one worker node is running

sources.quote: Recovery is performed by any live node; there is no single point of failure.

ears.when: a job changes state
ears.shall: record the transition with its timestamp, the node that made it and the reason

ears.when: an attempt fails
ears.shall: store the exception type, message and stack trace and the node that ran the attempt
never remove a dead-lettered job except when its retention expires or someone deletes it explicitly, and log every removal with the job id and name

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: RET-3's 'never silently deleted' means 'never without a trace', so the 30-day retention (STO-7) stays and every removal is logged and counted in a metric.

ears.shall: keep a job's state history, captured logs and parameters for exactly as long as the job itself
never use type names found in stored data to deserialize a payload, and resolve a job's handler only from the registered job name table

ears.when: a stored payload is read
ears.shall: ignore properties the job type no longer has and give missing properties their default values

ears.when: a job executes
ears.shall: resolve its handler and execution middleware in a dependency-injection scope created for that execution and dispose the scope, asynchronously where services support it, when the execution ends

ears.where: the same job metadata is set both by an attribute on the job type and fluently in AddBellhop
ears.shall: use the fluent value

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: the extension is confirmed; per-enqueue options override both the attribute and the fluent value (SCH-4, RET-1, REQ-100).

sources.quote: with fluent configuration winning

ears.shall: mask its value in the dashboard, captured logs and traces

ears.where: several applications share one store under different namespaces
ears.shall: never let a worker see or claim a job from another namespace

ears.when: its handler writes a log line through the job-scoped logger at or above the capture level
ears.shall: store the line with its timestamp, level, category and structured properties on the job, unless capture is disabled globally or for that job type

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: capture is on by default at Information and above, as BLT-1 says; DSH-6's 'opt-in' is superseded. It can be disabled globally or per job type, is capped per job (INV-126) and is removed with the job (INV-119).

sources.quote: Every line written to the job-scoped ILogger ... at or above a configurable level (default Information) is captured to the store

ears.shall: never store more than CapturedLogLimit of captured log lines per job, and mark the point where the log was truncated

ears.when: its handler reports progress with a fraction and an optional message
ears.shall: store the latest progress on the job

ears.when: a tag is set at enqueue, by an attribute on the job type, by enqueue middleware or by the running handler
ears.shall: store the tag on the job and add it to the job's secondary index

requirements.notes: Tags are 'key' or 'key:value' strings.

ears.when: a job is enqueued
ears.shall: capture a correlation id from the configured accessor when one is set, otherwise from the configured header when one is set, otherwise from the current Activity

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: explicit configuration beats ambient context.

ears.shall: give every continuation and every job enqueued from a handler the correlation id of its parent

ears.when: a job is enqueued, started, succeeds, fails, is dead-lettered or cancelled, or a recurring occurrence is missed
ears.shall: call every IJobEvents handler registered in dependency injection with the matching event, once, on the node that made the transition, after the store write has committed

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: recovery events are raised by the recovering node. A throwing event handler never changes the job (INV-136).

ears.when: an application adds a continuation to a parent job with the condition OnSuccess, OnFailure or OnCompletion
ears.shall: store the continuation as awaiting, with its parentId and condition

ears.when: its parent succeeds
ears.if: the condition is OnSuccess or OnCompletion
ears.shall: enqueue the continuation

ears.when: its parent is dead-lettered
ears.if: the condition is OnFailure or OnCompletion
ears.shall: enqueue the continuation

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 (reading confirmed): Failed (will retry) is not terminal, so OnFailure and OnCompletion fire on dead-lettering, not on each failed attempt.

ears.when: its parent is cancelled
ears.shall: cancel the continuation, whatever its condition

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: cancelling a parent cancels all its continuations, so 'completion' (REQ-171, REQ-172) means succeeded or dead-lettered, never cancelled. The cascade repeats down a chain.

ears.when: its parent succeeds
ears.if: the condition is OnFailure
ears.shall: cancel the continuation with reason ConditionNotMet

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: a continuation whose condition does not match resolves to Cancelled; the reason tells it apart from an operator cancel. Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-9 (recommended option 1): a continuation whose parent is dead-lettered and whose condition does not match stays awaiting, because the parent can still be requeued (REQ-141) and succeed, as batches already allow (REQ-179). It is cancelled when the parent is cancelled (REQ-173), deleted or removed by retention (REQ-188). Same event as REQ-171 with the complementary guard.

ears.when: an application adds a continuation to a parent that has already succeeded, been dead-lettered or been cancelled
ears.shall: resolve the continuation as if the parent had just finished (REQ-171 to REQ-174), and store it as awaiting only when none of those rules applies

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 (reading confirmed): without this, a continuation added after its parent finished would wait for an event that already happened and hang, violating LIV-102. refiner-model 2026-11-06 run 2 F-3 (recommended option): since run-1 F-9 a non-matching continuation of a dead-lettered parent stays awaiting (REQ-174), so one added after the parent was dead-lettered waits for a requeue too, exactly like one added before.

ears.shall: eventually enqueue or cancel it

requirements.notes: Expected to fail as written when the parent stays Unroutable or Failed for ever, and for an OnBatchSucceeded continuation of a batch that stays Completed (REQ-181). Deleting a parent now cancels its continuations (REQ-188), and retention only removes finished parents, whose continuations were already resolved. These are the findings we want the model to report. Confirmed by the model 2026-11-06 (F-13) behind an Unroutable parent and a Completed batch, and accepted; an operator can cancel the continuation (REQ-134). Since F-9 a continuation also waits behind a dead-lettered parent until it is requeued, cancelled, deleted or removed, so LIV-102 is a should.

sources.quote: never hang in Awaiting forever

ears.when: an application creates a chain of jobs
ears.shall: store the first job as enqueued and each later job as an OnSuccess continuation of the one before it, all in one store transaction, so that either the whole chain exists or none of it does

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 (reading confirmed): OnSuccess, so a dead-lettered step cancels the rest of the chain (REQ-174) and a cancelled step cancels it too (REQ-173). Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-9: a dead-lettered step now keeps the rest of the chain awaiting; requeuing the step and its success revives the chain (REQ-171). Cancelling, deleting or removing the step cancels the rest.

ears.when: an application creates a named batch of jobs
ears.shall: store the batch and all its member jobs in one store transaction

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: a batch is complete at creation; members cannot be added later (REQ-178 retired).

ears.when: an application adds jobs to it
ears.shall: add the jobs to the batch atomically

requirements.notes: Retired. Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: batches are closed at creation, so the race between extending a batch and its last member finishing cannot happen. WF-3's 'MAY be extended while open' is not taken up.

sources.quote: Batches MAY be extended while open.

ears.while: a batch is open or completed
ears.when: every member job has succeeded
ears.shall: mark the batch succeeded

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: Succeeded when every member succeeded. A Completed batch is upgraded to Succeeded if its failed members are later requeued and succeed; its OnBatchSucceeded continuations fire then (REQ-181). Each continuation still fires at most once.

ears.when: every member job is succeeded, dead-lettered, cancelled or deleted and at least one did not succeed
ears.shall: mark the batch completed

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: Completed means every member finished and at least one did not succeed. It is not final: see REQ-179. Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-10 (recommended option): a member deleted explicitly (REQ-144) counts as finished and not succeeded, so the batch still completes.

ears.when: its batch succeeds, or, for OnBatchCompleted only, its batch completes
ears.shall: enqueue the continuation

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: an OnBatchSucceeded continuation stays Awaiting while its batch is Completed, because the batch can still become Succeeded (REQ-179). It can therefore wait for ever, which LIV-102 will report; an operator can cancel it (REQ-134).

sources.quote: batch-level continuations (OnBatchSucceeded, OnBatchCompleted)

ears.when: an application schedules a job for a time that is not in the future according to the database clock, or with a zero or negative delay
ears.shall: store the job as enqueued at once, with scheduledAt recording the requested time, and return its job id

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: no wait for the next scheduler pass.

ears.shall: wait UnroutableAfter, 5 minutes by default, before marking an unclaimed job unroutable (UnroutableAfter)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: longer than a typical rolling deploy, short enough that a misspelt job name surfaces quickly.

ears.when: its handler returns without an exception
ears.if: the job returns a result larger than ResultSizeLimit
ears.shall: store no result, mark the result as dropped for size and log a warning with the size and the limit

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: the job still succeeds because the work was done; a truncated result would be invalid JSON. Same event as REQ-127 and REQ-128.

ears.shall: cap stored job results at ResultSizeLimit, 1 MB by default (ResultSizeLimit)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.while: a job is processing, its timeout token was signalled and its cancellation was not requested
ears.if: the handler is still running TimeoutGracePeriod later or throws OperationCanceledException within it, and the attempt number has reached maxAttempts or the retry policy declines another attempt
ears.shall: abandon the handler if it is still running and move the job to dead-lettered with reason Timeout

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: a timeout is an ordinary failure, so exhausted attempts dead-letter it. Complementary guard to REQ-138. Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-6 (recommended option): a job whose cancellation was requested is marked cancelled instead (REQ-136, REQ-190).

ears.shall: give a handler TimeoutGracePeriod, 30 seconds by default, after its timeout token is signalled before abandoning it (TimeoutGracePeriod)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.when: its parent is deleted or removed by retention, or, for a batch-level continuation, its batch is removed (REQ-192)
ears.shall: cancel the continuation

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06, so a deleted parent never leaves a continuation hanging (LIV-102). Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-9: removal by retention is included, because a dead-lettered parent now keeps its OnSuccess continuations awaiting until it is requeued or removed. Run 2 F-5: an OnBatchSucceeded continuation of a batch that stays Completed is cancelled when the batch is removed (REQ-192).

ears.if: a run presents a lease token that is no longer the job's current leaseToken when it renews the lease, reports progress, completes or fails
ears.shall: refuse the write, leave the job unchanged and log a stale-completion warning

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 (fencing). After a lease expires and another node recovers the job, the original run can no longer succeed, fail or extend it, so a job never ends twice or ends while it is Processing elsewhere. Worth adding later: a refused heartbeat could cancel the stale run's token.

ears.if: an application or operator requeues a job that is not succeeded, dead-lettered or cancelled, or whose unique key is held by another active job
ears.shall: refuse the request with an error and leave the job unchanged

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 for the state rule. The unique-key rule follows from INV-100: requeuing would otherwise create a second active job with the same key.

ears.if: an application or operator deletes a processing job
ears.shall: refuse the request with an error that says to cancel the job first, and leave the job unchanged

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.if: a handler throws
ears.shall: not retry the job

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: Inline runs a job once and rethrows (REQ-146).

ears.when: a job with continuations finishes
ears.shall: run the continuations that its outcome releases on the caller's thread before the enqueue call returns

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.when: an application schedules a job
ears.shall: store the job as scheduled without running it

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. Tests advance a fake TimeProvider to run it.

ears.shall: apply unique keys and concurrency keys as in the normal execution mode

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. A job whose concurrency key is held is deferred, not failed or blocked (INV-137).

ears.when: an application schedules a job with a unique key while an active job with the same key exists that is not scheduled
ears.if: the duplicate policy is ReplaceSchedule
ears.shall: create no job, change nothing and return the existing job's id with WasDuplicate set to true

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: behaves like Ignore once the existing job has left Scheduled.

ears.if: an IJobEvents handler throws
ears.shall: log the exception and leave the job's state unchanged

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: observers are never part of the state machine.

ears.if: a job is created while its concurrency key is held by Max running jobs
ears.shall: store the job as enqueued and run it inline on the thread of a job holding the key as soon as that job finishes, before the call that started the holding job returns

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. Applies to every call that creates a job (EnqueueAsync, EnqueueManyAsync, ContinueWithAsync, ChainAsync, batch creation, recurring trigger-now). Failing would make code that works in production fail under test, and blocking deadlocks when a handler enqueues a job with its own key. Example: handler A (key tenant:7, Max 1) enqueues B with the same key; B is stored and runs right after A, before the outer EnqueueAsync(A) returns. When two test threads collide, the second thread's call returns before its job has run, and that job runs on the first thread.

ears.shall: give every job a timeout of DefaultJobTimeout, 5 minutes, unless one is set by attribute, fluently or per enqueue (DefaultJobTimeout)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. The source gave no default. A handler that ignores its token is abandoned TimeoutGracePeriod later (REQ-138, REQ-186). The docs must say so prominently, because a job that silently ran for an hour under another library will now time out.

ears.while: a job is processing and its cancellation was requested
ears.when: its lease expires with attempts left, its node releases it at shutdown, its handler is still running TimeoutGracePeriod after its timeout token was signalled, or its handler throws an exception other than OperationCanceledException or PermanentJobFailureException while the attempt number is below maxAttempts and the retry policy allows another attempt
ears.shall: abandon the handler if it is still running and mark the job cancelled instead of returning it to enqueued, marking it failed or dead-lettering it for the timeout

requirements.notes: Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-7 (recommended option): a cancellation request recorded by REQ-135 is never lost when the job leaves processing some other way, so a cancelled job does not run again. The guards of REQ-129, REQ-132, REQ-138, REQ-140 and REQ-186 exclude a requested cancellation, so exactly one rule applies. Exhausted attempts on a handler exception or lease expiry still dead-letter (REQ-131, REQ-133), because a dead-lettered job does not run again. Run 2 F-1 (recommended option): the exception branch covers exactly the failures REQ-129 would retry. A failure that would dead-letter (attempts used up, the retry policy declines, or a PermanentJobFailureException) still dead-letters under REQ-131: a cancel request stops the next attempt, it does not rewrite how this attempt ended.

ears.when: the system abandons a handler that is still running, after a timeout (REQ-138, REQ-186, REQ-190) or a release at shutdown (REQ-140), or refuses the heartbeat of a handler that is still running because its lease token is no longer current (INV-128)
ears.shall: log a warning naming the job, its attempt and the node, and record in that attempt that its handler was abandoned or lost its lease and is still running outside the node's concurrency limit

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-5: abandoned handlers run outside the node's limit (INV-106) and are made visible rather than counted. Run 2 F-7 (recommended option): a handler whose lease was lost (a partition or long pause, then recovery by another node) is the third way a node keeps running a handler it no longer holds a claim for, so it is recorded the same way; the node claims again as soon as it holds fewer claims than its limit (REQ-123).

ears.while: a batch is completed or succeeded
ears.when: every member job that is still stored has been succeeded, cancelled or dead-lettered for longer than that state's retention
ears.shall: remove the batch together with those member jobs, their state history, captured logs and parameters

requirements.rationale: REQ-145 keeps the members of a completed batch so it can still be upgraded (REQ-179), and nothing ended that protection: a batch with one dead letter nobody requeued was kept for ever, payloads and logs included.
requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 run 2 F-5 (recommended option). Members stay requeueable until every one of them is past its own retention, measured from when it last finished, so requeuing a member postpones the removal. Covers succeeded batches too, whose members REQ-145 removes one by one: the batch record goes with the last of them. Awaiting batch-level continuations are cancelled by REQ-188.

ears.if: an application adds a continuation to a parent job id that does not exist
ears.shall: reject the call with an error that names the parent id, and store nothing

requirements.notes: Resolved after refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-11 (recommended option): a parent that was deleted or removed by retention falls between REQ-170, REQ-175 and REQ-188 and would leave the continuation awaiting for ever.

scenarios.title: Fire-and-forget happy path
scenarios.given: One running node with a free worker; queue default is active; handler for send-welcome-email is registered.
scenarios.then: The job is Succeeded with attempt 1 and three recorded transitions.

scenarios.title: Retries until dead-lettered
scenarios.given: A job whose handler always throws; maxAttempts = 2.
scenarios.then: The job is DeadLettered with two stored attempts, each with exception details and node.

scenarios.title: Node crash is recovered by another node
scenarios.given: Nodes A and B running; job j enqueued; maxAttempts = 5.

steps.note: A crashes; lease expires; B recovers j as Interrupted

scenarios.then: j is Succeeded, its history shows one Interrupted attempt by A and attempt 2 by B.

scenarios.title: Healthy long-running job is never recovered
scenarios.given: Job j is processing on node A for ten times LeaseDuration and A's heartbeats keep succeeding.

steps.note: node B tries to recover j

scenarios.title: Second worker cannot claim a claimed job
scenarios.given: Job j is enqueued; nodes A and B both have free workers.

scenarios.title: Duplicate unique key returns the existing job
scenarios.given: No jobs exist; policy Ignore.

steps.note: enqueue again with UniqueKey = order-42 on another node

scenarios.then: Exactly one active job has key order-42 and the second call returned its id with WasDuplicate = true.

scenarios.title: Concurrency key mutex blocks a second job
scenarios.given: Jobs j1 and j2 are enqueued with concurrency key tenant:7 and Max = 1; two free workers.

steps.note: j2 claim attempted while j1 processing

scenarios.title: Cancelled scheduled job never runs
scenarios.given: Job j is scheduled for tomorrow.

scenarios.title: OnFailure continuation runs after dead-letter
scenarios.given: Parent p has maxAttempts = 1; continuation c is OnFailure of p.
scenarios.then: p is DeadLettered and c is Enqueued.

scenarios.title: OnSuccess continuation does not run after dead-letter
scenarios.given: Parent p has maxAttempts = 1; continuation c is OnSuccess of p.

steps.note: c would be enqueued as if p succeeded

scenarios.title: Paused queue is not drained
scenarios.given: Job j is enqueued in queue reports; a free worker serves reports.

scenarios.title: Unroutable job resumes when its handler appears
scenarios.given: Job j named old-report is enqueued; no running node has a handler for it.

steps.note: UnroutableAfter passes and no live node lists old-report; j becomes Unroutable
a node starts that has a handler with alias old-report

scenarios.then: j is Succeeded and was never Failed or DeadLettered.

scenarios.title: Requeued dead letter starts again from attempt one
scenarios.given: Job j is DeadLettered after 5 attempts.

scenarios.title: Rolled-back transactional enqueue never runs
scenarios.given: PostgreSQL store sharing the application database; app enqueues j inside its transaction and then rolls the transaction back.

steps.note: a worker tries to claim j after the rollback

scenarios.title: Batch success releases its continuation
scenarios.given: Batch b has members j1 and j2 and an OnBatchSucceeded continuation c.
scenarios.then: b is Succeeded and c is Enqueued exactly once.

scenarios.title: Shutdown hands an unfinished job to another node
scenarios.given: Node A is processing j, whose handler ignores cancellation; node B is running.

steps.note: A is draining, ShutdownTimeout passes, token cancelled

scenarios.then: j is Processing on B with attempt 1; the run interrupted by shutdown was not counted.

scenarios.title: Oversized payload is rejected
scenarios.given: PayloadHardLimit = 1 MB; the app enqueues a job with a 2 MB payload.

scenarios.title: Stale run cannot complete a recovered job
scenarios.given: Nodes A and B running; job j enqueued; maxAttempts = 5. A is partitioned from the store long enough for its lease to expire.

steps.note: A claims j with token t1
lease expires; B recovers j as Interrupted
B claims j with token t2
A's handler returns and tries to mark j succeeded with t1

scenarios.title: Cancelling a parent cancels its OnCompletion continuation
scenarios.given: Parent p is scheduled for tomorrow; continuation c is OnCompletion of p.
scenarios.then: p and c are Cancelled and c was never Enqueued.

scenarios.title: Completed batch is upgraded after a requeue
scenarios.given: Batch b has members j1 and j2 with maxAttempts = 1 and an OnBatchSucceeded continuation c.
scenarios.then: b is Succeeded and c is Enqueued exactly once.

scenarios.title: A process without a worker never runs jobs
scenarios.given: A web API registers AddBellhop with the client and maps the dashboard, without AddWorker; job j is enqueued and its handler is registered there.

steps.note: the web API process tries to claim j

scenarios.title: Requeuing a dead-lettered chain step revives the chain
scenarios.given: A chain import then report; import has maxAttempts = 1 and its handler throws once, then succeeds.

steps.note: chain created: import enqueued, report awaiting
import throws and is dead-lettered; report stays awaiting

scenarios.then: report is Enqueued and the chain continues without the operator touching report.

scenarios.title: A cancellation survives lease expiry
scenarios.given: Node A is processing j1 with attempts left and is cut off from the store; node B is running.

steps.note: operator cancels j1; the request is recorded

scenarios.then: j1 is Cancelled and is never claimed again.

scenarios.title: A continuation of a missing parent is rejected
scenarios.given: Job j1 succeeded and was removed by retention.

steps.note: the app adds an OnSuccess continuation to j1's id

features.name: Captured logs, progress, tags, correlation and events

glossary.MaxAttempts: Total attempts before dead-lettering; 5 by default (REQ-100).
glossary.LeaseDuration: How long a claim stays valid without a heartbeat; 60 s by default (REQ-102).
glossary.PollInterval: Idle polling interval; 1 s by default (REQ-103).
glossary.PayloadSoftLimit: 64 KB; above it enqueue logs a warning (REQ-105).
glossary.PayloadHardLimit: 1 MB (256 KB on Redis); above it enqueue is rejected (REQ-105, REQ-513).
glossary.CapturedLogLimit: 256 KB of captured log lines per job (REQ-108).
glossary.TimeoutGracePeriod: Time a handler gets after its timeout token is signalled before it is abandoned; 30 s by default (REQ-187).
glossary.ResultSizeLimit: Cap on a stored job result; 1 MB by default (REQ-185).
glossary.DefaultJobTimeout: Timeout of a job that sets none; 5 min (REQ-189).
glossary.UnroutableAfter: How long an unclaimed job waits before it can be marked Unroutable; 5 min by default (REQ-183).
glossary.active: For uniqueness: Scheduled, Enqueued, Processing, Awaiting, Failed or Unroutable (REQ-107).
